expectedFailures.name: test_registry_audit_snapshot_is_current_and_honest_about_open_gaps
expectedFailures.message: 2026-09-07: `term_explanation` joined the registry, so the source manifest carries a module this sealed summary does not -- its module list has shifted, not just its count. Regenerating it is `make audit-registry-real-data`, which runs every direct module test and rewrites a sealed evidence artifact, which needs the owner's own words to the session performing it. PARKED, NOT FORGOTTEN: no consumer build needs it, and it runs serially (the tool runs `sys.executable -m pytest` with no -n; the direct module tests alone recorded 1,194 s in the committed summary) under the shared measurement lock, `compositions/measurement.lock` in the SpicySearch checkout whose AGENTS.md states the rule, so it runs in any quiet window in which no lane needs that lock -- never mid-batch. The complete suite is NOT part of the run: the tool reaches it only when the gate has no failures, and the gate will have them. What is derivable before running: from the current manifest and `real_data_evidence_failures`, the gate stays `failed` and gains exactly one evidence-derived gap, term_explanation's, which has no publisher input of its own by design; the receipt-derived gaps are observed by the run and cannot be predicted. THREE TRAPS FOR WHOEVER RUNS IT: plain `verify_registry_audit.py` writes realDataGate {status: notEvaluated, failures: []} over a summary that honestly says `failed` with named gaps; only the --require-real-data form (the make target's) preserves them. The audit aborts WITHOUT WRITING when a direct test fails, which reads exactly like a stale summary. And on the SUCCESSFUL path the target still exits 1, printing `registry audit error: real-data gate failed` AFTER writing, while the not-written case prints `direct registry tests failed with exit code N` -- read the message, never the exit code or the mtime. STRICT so the marker cannot outlive the regeneration.
